content.title: Current status and intended use of this page
content.body: Around was a lightweight video-calling application for hybrid and remote teams. It is no longer a current standalone product: reporting published in January 2025 said the service would cease operations on March 31, 2025 after Miro acquired it, and Miro's marketplace listing now marks the Around app as deprecated. This page is retained as a historical product record and migration reference, not as a recommendation to sign up or adopt the old service. Sources: https://alternativeto.net/news/2025/1/the-video-call-app-around-is-shutting-down-just-over-a-year-after-its-acquisition-by-miro/ and https://miro.com/marketplace/around-by-miro-labs/.

content.title: What made the product distinctive
content.body: Archived descriptions emphasized a lightweight call interface with small floating video bubbles that could remain visible while a person worked in other applications. The design aimed to make remote conversations feel more informal than a full-screen meeting grid. Historical descriptions also mention playful meeting interactions and tools intended to support spontaneous collaboration. Because the standalone service is discontinued, these details should be treated as a record of the product's former positioning rather than a current capability checklist.

content.title: What former users should verify
content.body: If an organization previously used Around, the practical task is to confirm whether any accounts, recordings, meeting notes, or workflow references still exist in internal documentation. Do not assume that old meeting links or recordings remain accessible. Review the current Miro documentation for any successor features and confirm which historical workflows, if any, can be recreated in an active product. The current marketplace listing identifies the Around app as deprecated; it is not evidence that the standalone service can be used today.

content.title: Choosing an active replacement
content.body: Select a replacement by matching the meeting scenario rather than trying to reproduce every old interface detail. For routine team calls, compare active meeting products on participant access, calendar integration, screen sharing, recording, accessibility, security controls, administration, and support. For workshops that rely on a shared canvas, evaluate a collaboration platform's current meeting features directly. Test the same meeting scenario in two active candidates and document what the team gains or loses.

content.title: Migration and operational cleanup
content.body: Check internal links, meeting templates, onboarding documents, calendar descriptions, and team playbooks for references to the retired service. Replace old booking or meeting instructions with a currently supported workflow and verify the new link end to end. If any data recovery is still needed, consult current Miro support materials rather than relying on archived instructions from third-party directories. Avoid entering credentials or downloading software from unofficial mirrors.

content.title: Historical rating and pricing status
content.body: No current price, current plan, or active user-rating aggregate is published here because the standalone product is discontinued and an auditable current source trail is not available. The review preserves product history and replacement criteria rather than inventing a live rating or pretending that the old service can still be purchased. The appropriate decision for new deployments is to evaluate an active alternative.

content.title: Replacement requirements
content.body: Write down which historical Around workflows mattered most: spontaneous calls, a compact video interface, quick screen sharing, or easy access from a shared workspace. Separate essential requirements from preferences that were specific to the retired product. Use that list to compare active services rather than searching for an exact clone of an interface that is no longer supported.

content.title: Link and account cleanup
content.body: Audit internal meeting templates, onboarding documents, calendar descriptions, and team playbooks for links to the old service. Replace each with a currently supported meeting path and test it from a normal user account. Confirm whether any needed records or recordings were preserved before shutdown; do not assume an old link still works. Avoid unofficial downloads or mirrors of the retired app.

content.title: Historical evaluation checklist
content.body: For teams documenting a past deployment, record the former use case, which workflows must be replaced, and any known data-retention questions. For a new deployment, compare active candidates on joining a call, screen sharing, calendar behavior, recording, accessibility, administration, and support. No numeric score is published for the discontinued service because current availability and pricing do not apply.

content.title: Migration checklist
content.body: Use this checklist when retiring an old Around workflow.
items: Find old meeting links and templates.
Choose an active replacement and test a real call.
Confirm any required records were preserved.
Review the replacement's access and recording controls.
Tell users when the old workflow should no longer be used.

faqs.question: Can a team still adopt Around?
faqs.answer: No. Around's standalone video-calling service was discontinued in 2025. This page is historical and is not a recommendation to adopt it.

faqs.question: Why is this review still available?
faqs.answer: It provides historical context for users who encounter old Around references and gives a checklist for selecting a currently supported replacement.

faqs.question: What happened to Around's Miro connection?
faqs.answer: Miro's marketplace listing for Around by Miro Labs now marks the app as deprecated. Check Miro's current documentation for any successor functionality.

faqs.question: Does PilotStack publish a current Around rating or price?
faqs.answer: No. The product is discontinued, so no current price or active third-party rating is asserted.
